title: Review and Reset Your Budget
blurb: Use a short monthly review to keep your plan useful.
cards: Plan the month, track a few key categories, then review what happened. The review is where you learn whether the plan matched your real costs.
What went as expected? What changed? What is one adjustment for next month? Keep what worked and change only what needs changing.
Adjust the amount and rebalance another category
A realistic adjustment helps the plan match life.
The same mismatch will likely continue.
When is a budget review most useful?
Only when you make a mistake
Regularly, so you can respond to changes
Only at the end of the year
A regular quick review helps you catch changes while there is still time to adjust.
What is a good next step after noticing a realistic plan was too strict?
Small revisions make a budget more sustainable.
example: Your grocery plan was $250, but recent receipts show $300 is more realistic. Raise groceries by $50 and choose another flexible category to adjust.
